title: Play Store Download Pending, App Crashes and Overheating: Fixes
html:
These three problems have different fixes, so start with the heading that matches yours. For a stuck Play Store download, check the connection, storage, updates and the date and time. For an app that crashes, update it, clear its cache, and reinstall it if needed. For a phone that gets too hot, stop what it is doing, take it out of the sun, and let it cool down.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Menu names vary by brand and Android version; use the Settings search box if you cannot find one.

I went through the screens in these steps on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14, security update January 2025) on 11 Oct 2026.

Play Store download stuck on "Pending"

Google's help page lists six basic checks. Do them in this order:

  1. Connection. Use a strong connection, ideally Wi-Fi.
  2. Storage. Open Settings, then Storage. Google treats less than 1 GB free as low space, and low space can stop apps from downloading.
  3. Android update. Settings, then System, then Software update, then System update.
  4. Restart the Play Store. Swipe up from the bottom, swipe the Play Store card away to close it, and open it again.
  5. Restart the phone.
  6. Date and time. Settings, then System, then Date and time. Turn on "Set time automatically" and the automatic time zone option.

If the download is still stuck after all six, Google's page points to its advanced troubleshooting steps.

An app keeps crashing

Google's order for an installed app that is not working:

  1. Restart the phone and check for an Android update (Settings, then System, then Software update).
  2. Update the app. Play Store, profile picture, Manage apps and device, then Updates available.
  3. Force stop the app, then open it again. The Force stop button is on the app's info page in Settings, under Apps.
  4. Clear its cache, then its data. Both are in Settings under Apps, in the app's Storage section. Clearing the cache removes temporary files. Clearing the data resets the app, which signs you out and removes what it saved on the phone, so back up anything important first.
  5. Check the date and time are set automatically.
  6. Uninstall and reinstall. Touch and hold the app, then remove it, and install it again from the Play Store.

If many apps crash, or the crashes started right after you installed something new, use Safe mode to find the cause. It is explained in our Safe mode guide. If the phone is slow as well, see why your Android phone is slow.

The phone is too hot

Google's Pixel help says a phone can feel warm during normal use, for example while you play videos or games, record HD video, use a hotspot, or while it is transferring data or being set up. When it gets too hot, the phone protects itself. It can slow down, limit charging speed, turn off the camera flash or go into low power mode, and if the temperature keeps rising it can turn itself off.

If it is too hot right now:

  1. Unplug it if it is charging.
  2. Move it somewhere cooler.
  3. Do not use it until it has cooled down.

To stop it happening again, Google suggests avoiding heavy apps (video calls, navigation, streaming) while charging, keeping the phone out of hot cars and direct sun, not leaving it somewhere enclosed or badly ventilated, lowering the brightness, using a case made for your model, and using Wi-Fi instead of mobile data where you can.

On a Pixel 6 or newer you can check the temperature yourself: Settings, then Battery, then Battery diagnostics, then "Phone is very warm". If it is hot even when you are doing nothing, that points to an app or a fault, so read our battery drain guide as well.

What to do next

  1. Stuck download: connection, storage, update, restart, date and time.
  2. Crashing app: update it, clear cache, clear data, reinstall.
  3. Hot phone: unplug, cool down, then cut heavy use while charging.
  4. If a problem comes back after all of this, see a service centre.
